editorial:
Imagine sitting down for a movie and getting two different comedies for the price of one. That is exactly what you get here. The first half follows a guy who stutters and spends most of his time struggling to say the right words while trying to win over a woman he really likes. It is a classic setup that relies on awkward moments and funny misunderstandings. Then, the movie shifts gears entirely to a story starring the great Renato Pozzetto. He plays a gay man living with a very dramatic partner, but things get messy when he starts falling for a woman. He has no idea how to break the news to his boyfriend without causing a total meltdown, which leads to some hilarious chaos.

What really makes this work is Pozzetto's timing; he knows exactly how to play the straight man in a ridiculous situation. While the two stories feel separate, they both bring a lighthearted, silly energy that keeps you smiling. If you enjoy old-school Italian humor that does not take itself too seriously, you will love this. It is a great pick for a lazy weekend. You should try to find it for rent on Apple TV or grab the Blu-ray for your physical collection to keep the quality crisp and clear.
endingExplained: The first story ends with the stuttering man finally finding his confidence and winning over his love interest through honesty. In the second story, the tension peaks as the main character tries to balance his feelings. After plenty of dramatic arguments and funny mishaps, he eventually finds a way to resolve the conflict with his partner. The movie wraps up on a light note, showing that love is messy and confusing no matter who you are.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves vintage Italian comedies and awkward romantic situations.
